Inference cost economics (the price war became the dominant frame — GPT-5.6 Luna down ~80% and Terra 20% with Fast mode replacing Priority Processing, DeepSeek V4-Flash-0731 already beating Luna on price-per-task by roughly 2x on independent analysis, and after a year of only-rising prices practitioners recomputing cost-per-task live against GLM 5.2, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek; OmniRoute adds +7,063 in a week)

MCP adoption & the 2026-07-28 spec (a Swiss private bank writes 'standards such as the Model Context Protocol' into a job description as a delivery requirement; Snowflake ships the enforcement point at the warehouse boundary rather than the protocol; a 25-year SAP integrator benchmarks MCP against RFC/PI-PO/BTP)

Inference cost economics (a menial Amazon coding project ran 860% over its Claude allocation — $1.8M across five months, undetected, and it failed anyway; insiders describe mistakes that were trivially cheap under seat pricing becoming catastrophically expensive under token metering; NVIDIA argues the KV cache for long-context agent sessions has moved past system memory, making storage a first-order determinant of inference economics)

Agentic retrieval & RAG architecture (Pinecone's Nexus compiles scattered documents into a knowledge layer agents query directly instead of re-retrieving per call, with KnowQL putting intent, provenance, output shape, confidence and *budget* in one declarative call; HALT makes the stopping decision verification-aware; a companion paper finds most agentic-RAG errors happen before any evidence is retrieved)

MCP adoption & the 2026-07-28 spec (no MCP or A2A spec news at all today — the news collector's own theme balance records a zero — and the protocol surfaces instead through its consequences: a stateless core with authorization deferred to extensions, a Medium piece arguing shell-out-to-CLI versus protocol-mediated tool access is still a live debate, and 143k vulnerabilities in the server population)

Inference cost economics (Sandisk and SK hynix publish the first OCP specification for High Bandwidth Flash — a vendor-neutral tier between HBM and SSD, 512GB modules at 0.4–3.0 TB/s, with Google and Tenstorrent joining during standardisation — which is the concrete follow-through on the argument that storage becomes the inference bottleneck once KV caches outgrow system memory; on the demand side Pinecone makes budget a first-class query primitive)

Agentic retrieval / RAG-as-decision-loop (the RAG default is under attack from three sides at once - Sierra's Context Engine compiles what a business knows into a stateful context layer, InsightEmb trains embeddings on action intent rather than surface text, and the vectorless-RAG argument says structured data never needed similarity search; HN's best taxonomy of the day says agentic search today is late-interaction retrieval, a smarter harness, or just grep)

MCP adoption & the 2026-07-28 stateless rewrite (the biggest change since launch - sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header are gone so any instance behind an ordinary load balancer answers any request, Tasks moves to an extension, Roots/Sampling/Logging are deprecated, and the SDKs have passed 1B cumulative downloads; Snowflake governs 100+ MCP servers, Salesforce ships Tableau MCP, ServiceNow GAs Action Fabric's MCP server, and a business-aviation employer writes MCP into a JD)

Inference cost economics (AMD buys Taalas to etch model weights directly into silicon - an explicit moat play against commoditization by Chinese open-weight models, with the obvious counter running through the replies that etched weights cannot be updated so the economics only work if model churn slows; meanwhile the effort dial ships as a product control, DeepSeek warns of a price rise, and a small open model does retrieval at 1/100th the cost)

MCP adoption (the 2026-07-28 revision is FINAL — transport-level session management removed outright, so an MCP server is now an ordinary stateless HTTP workload behind a normal load balancer, gateway or WAF; plus Multi Round-Trip Requests, header-based routing, cacheable list results, a formal Extensions framework and a deprecation policy, with the TypeScript and Python SDKs each past 1bn cumulative downloads and Google shipping a migration guide)

AI security & offensive-security agents (Stealing Reasoning Traces at 684 pts, OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber and the Daybreak expansion for vetted defenders, mass vulnerability scans spoofing ClaudeBot, Eugene Yan on cybersecurity evals)
